newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU presidency says no EMU without Germany, France.
newsitem.headline: EU presidency says no EMU without Germany, France.

text.p: The Dutch presidency of the European Union on Wednesday ruled out the prospect of a single currency without Germany or France, but stressed EMU budgetary criteria must not be relaxed in the interests of expediency.
"I see no political basis for beginning European Monetary Union if France or Germany do not take part," Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok told a news briefing.
"European Monetary Union without (either or both) is a non-starter," he stressed.

But Kok also warned against relaxing the strict deficit, national debt and inflation criteria on EMU entry, saying the January 1, 1999 deadline for the start of a single currency should not be allowed to dictate entry conditions.
"I am against delay (in starting EMU) and think that speculation about a delayed introduction is harmful," Kok said.
But he added, "I do not think that fear of a delayed introduction of the euro should lead to softened criteria... The timetable must not be allowed to dictate the criteria."
"I have always said (they) should be strictly maintained in order to safeguard the solidity and soundness of the...euro."
